{{Short description|Dutch optics engineer and professor}}
'''Joseph J.M. Braat''' (born 5 November 1946) is a Dutch [[Optical engineering|optics engineer]] and scientist. Between 1973 and 1998 he worked at [[Philips Natuurkundig Laboratorium|Philips Research Laboratories]]. He was professor of [[optics]] at [[Delft University of Technology]] between 1998 and 2008.

==Career==
Braat was born in [[Breda]] on 5 November 1946.<ref name="KaaKaa2008">{{cite book|author1=D. J. van de Kaa|author2=Kaa|author3=Y. de Roo|title=De Leden Van de Koninklijke Nederlandse Akademie Van Wetenschappen: Een Demografisch Perspectief: 1808 Tot 2008|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gzNvCGJEGCYC&pg=PA260|date=19 December 2008|publisher=Amsterdam University Press|isbn=978-90-6984-552-4|page=260}}</ref> He studied physics at [[Delft University of Technology]]. After his graduation he moved to France to work at the coherent optics group of Serge Lowenthal at the [[École supérieure d'optique|Institut d'Optique]] in Orsay. His PhD thesis was on [[holography]] using spatially incoherent light. In 1973 Braat returned to the Netherlands to work at [[Philips Natuurkundig Laboratorium|Philips Research Laboratories]]. There he contributed to early research on [[optical disc]] systems.<ref name=tud>{{cite web|author= |url=http://optics.smethods.eu/en/research/researchgroups/optics-research-group/people/guests/prof-dr-ir-jjm-braat/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180107110515/http://optics.smethods.eu/en/research/researchgroups/optics-research-group/people/guests/prof-dr-ir-jjm-braat/index.html |title=Prof. dr ir J.J.M. Braat |publisher=Delft University of Technology |date= |archive-date=7 January 2018}}</ref><ref name=fi>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.fi.edu/laureates/joseph-braat |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170214123154/https://www.fi.edu/laureates/joseph-braat |title=Joseph Braat |publisher=[[Franklin Institute]] |date=2001 |archive-date=14 February 2017}}</ref> During this period he developed a theory together with [[Harold Hopkins (physicist)|Harold Hopkins]] and Gijs Bouwhuis on the read-out of optical discs through [[Diffraction|diffraction of light]] by the information carrying disc structure.<ref name="mauve">{{cite web|author=Karen Mauve |url=https://www.hagenbeuk.nl/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/1998AfscheidBraat19-06.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180107111321/https://www.hagenbeuk.nl/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/1998AfscheidBraat19-06.pdf |title=Joseph Braat: verlaat het lab |language=Dutch |publisher=Hagenbeuk.nl |date=19 June 1998 |archive-date=7 January 2018}}</ref> He also contributed to the design of light paths for optical disc systems. At Philips Research Laboratories Braat contributed to [[lens]] and [[Systems design|system design]] for early [[Photolithography|photolithographic]] systems by Philips and [[ASML Holding|ASML]].<ref name="tud"/><ref name="mauve"/>

In 1988 Braat became a part-time professor of [[geometrical optics]] at [[Delft University of Technology]]. In 1998 he became a full professor of [[optics]]. During this time he performed research on [[extreme ultraviolet lithography]], optical [[aperture synthesis]] for astronomy, high density [[optical recording]], Extended Nijboer-Zernike theory and [[Terahertz nondestructive evaluation#Terahertz imaging|Terahertz imaging]].<ref name="tud"/><ref name="fi"/><ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.nijboerzernike.nl/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804075338/https://www.nijboerzernike.nl/ |title=Extended Nijboer-Zernike (ENZ) Analysis & Aberration Retrieval |publisher=nijboerzernike.nl |date=7 November 2019 |archive-date=4 August 2020}}</ref> In 1991 Braat was one of the founders of the [[European Optical Society]]. From 2004 to 2006 he served as its President.<ref name=tud/> Braat retired as professor in 2008.<ref name="tud"/>

In 1994 Braat won the Edward Longstreth Medal for Computer and Cognitive Science of the [[Franklin Institute]] for "contributions to optical data recording and design of aspherical objective lenses for read-out systems of optical storage".<ref name=fi/> Braat was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2001.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://knaw.nl/en/members/members/5219 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180106230007/https://knaw.nl/en/members/members/5219 |title=Joseph Braat |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=6 January 2018}}</ref> He became a Fellow of the European Optical Society in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.europeanoptics.org/pages/distinctions/eos-fellows.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200613233341/https://www.europeanoptics.org/pages/distinctions/eos-fellows.html |title=EOS fellows |publisher=European Optical Society |date= |archive-date=13 June 2020}}</ref> In 2019 he received the [[Gilles Holst|Holst]] Memorial Lecture Award from [[Eindhoven University of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tudelft.nl/2019/tnw/joseph-braat-receives-the-holst-award-medal-from-tue-rector-frank-baaijens |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220704032412/https://www.tudelft.nl/2019/tnw/joseph-braat-receives-the-holst-award-medal-from-tue-rector-frank-baaijens/ |title=Joseph Braat receives the Holst award medal from TU/e Rector Frank Baaijens |publisher=Delft University of Technology |date=9 December 2019 |archive-date=4 July 2022}}</ref>

Braat has received 60 US patents.<ref name=tud/>

== Bibliography ==
Braat is the author or co-author of some 150 scientific publications.<ref name=tud/> His main work is the 1000-page textbook ''Imaging Optics,'' which also contains contribution from second author Peter Török.<ref name="textbook">{{cite web|url=https://www.tudelft.nl/2019/tnw/book-launch-imaging-optics-by-joseph-braat-and-peter-toeroek/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201010082534/https://www.tudelft.nl/2019/tnw/book-launch-imaging-optics-by-joseph-braat-and-peter-toeroek/ |title=Book launch: "Imaging Optics" by Joseph Braat and Peter Török |publisher=Delft University of Technology |date=8 May 2019 |archive-date=10 October 2020}}</ref>

=== Books ===

* G. Bouwhuis, J. Braat, A. Huijser, J. Pasman, G. van Rosmalen, K.A.S. Immink, ''Principles of Optical Disc Systems'', Hilger, Bristol, UK (1985).
* J. Braat, P. Török, ''Imaging Optics'', Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, UK (2019).<ref name="textbook"/>
